Colour flextable cells by value

Source: R/flextable.R
phw_flextable_heat.Rd

Fills cells in the given columns with a PHW sequential palette, the way PHW heat tables do, and picks white or dark text automatically so values stay readable.

Usage

phw_flextable_heat(
  x,
  j,
  palette = "teals",
  domain = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  higher_is_better = TRUE,
  symbols = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A flextable.

j

Columns to colour, chosen as in dplyr::select(): unquoted names such as c(rate, cases), positions such as 2:5, or strings.

palette

A sequential or diverging palette name, a vector of colours, "rag" or "rag_accessible" (navy instead of green).

domain

Range of values the palette spans. Defaults to the range of the selected columns.

breaks

For palette = "rag": two cut points (red below the first, green at or above the second).

higher_is_better

For "rag": is a high value good (green)?

symbols

For "rag": add a shape before each value (a down triangle for red, a square for amber, an up triangle for green)?

Value

A flextable.

Details

For palette = "rag", colour alone doesn't work for colour-blind readers or in black-and-white print, so symbols = TRUE (the default) adds a shape before each value as well.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  rates <- data.frame(Area = paste("Area", LETTERS[1:4]),
                      `2024` = c(3.2, 1.5, 3.8, 2.3), `2025` = c(4.4, 0.7, 4.2, 0.2),
                      check.names = FALSE)
  phw_flextable(rates) |>
    phw_flextable_heat(j = 2:3)

  # Red, amber and green, with a shape in each cell as a second cue
  uptake <- data.frame(Area = paste("Area", LETTERS[1:4]),
                       Uptake = c(0.96, 0.93, 0.91, 0.95))
  phw_flextable(uptake, digits = 2) |>
    phw_flextable_heat(Uptake, palette = "rag_accessible", breaks = c(0.92, 0.95))
}
